text:
sara: heads up — we saw a spike in evictions in us-west2 during the overnight batch window. a bunch of preemptible GPUs dropped and some streaming requests lost KV state. wondering whether we should flip the drain window to 15s -> 45s and force a token-stream cutover earlier?

leo: can you paste the eviction pattern? is it short (<30s) or long flaky?

sara: mostly 20-40s notices, a few ~5s sudden kills. here's sample from the node event stream: 
```
NODE_ID=i-0abcd evict: type=preemptible notice_ms=22000 reason=spot-rebalance
NODE_ID=i-0efgh evict: type=preemptible notice_ms=4800 reason=host-maintenance
```

dmitri: 5s is brutal for graceful flush. we rely on two mechanisms: 1) preemptible drain handshake to finish active streaming tokens (up to drain_ms) then requeue inflight requests, 2) token-prefix caching so short cutovers don't drop full KV. both need tuning.

leo: proposal: set drain_ms=45000 for us-west2, enable aggressive requeue with immediate handoff to warm-on-demand pool after 30s. fallback policy: if handshake fails, fast token-swap and replay from prefix cache. thoughts? :thinking_face:

sara: that would reduce lost tokens but increases tail latency for unaffected requests. we should scope to streaming-heavy routes only (/v1/stream, /v1/kv-append).

dmitri: agree — routing policy needs to be route-level. sample config snippet: 
```yaml
preemptible_eviction:
  routes:
    - path: "/v1/stream"
      drain_ms: 45000
      requeue_policy: immediate_handoff
      fallback: token_prefix_replay
    - path: "/v1/embedding"
      drain_ms: 15000
      requeue_policy: best_effort
```

sara: how do we implement immediate_handoff? do we trust Dedicated warm pool IPs in same AZ or cross-AZ fallback? cross-AZ adds latency but reduces failure.

leo: start AZ-local warm on-demand first, if capacity not found within 8s then cross-AZ with higher cost. handoff sequence: 
1) runtime pauses accepting new fragments on preemptible node
2) token exporter sends last prefix to handoff target 
3) router rewrites connection -> on-demand endpoint 

(small command to test handoff:)
```bash
curl -X POST https://router.internal/handoff -d '{"session":"s-123","target":"on-demand-usw2a"}'
```

oncall-bot: detected 7 evictions in us-west2 in last 10m, average notice_ms=21000, median=19000.

dmitri: metrics we need to watch after rollout: %requests requeued, tail-p90 latency on /v1/stream, dropped-token-rate, cost-per-token (on-demand bump). set alert if dropped-token-rate > 0.1% for 5m.

sara: also add a short-lived SLO forgiveness window during the deployment (5m). ops-runbooks: include steps to toggle route-level drain and rollback.

leo: i'll prototype the router rewrite + handoff script today and run a canary on staging. will add a lint check to prevent global drain_ms edits without a risk signoff. :thumbsup:

dmitri: one more thought — enable soft-evict caching: extend KV prefix retention for 60s on preemptible nodes so a late handoff can still replay locally. low-cost change.

sara: good call. plan:
- leo: prototype handoff script + canary (today)
- dmitri: add route-level config + prefix retention (tomorrow)
- ops: add alerts and runbook entries
- deploy to us-west2 staging canary, monitor oncall-bot alerts for 1h before global roll

sara: tagging for follow-up @leo @dmitri. thanks everyone.

evict-bot: scheduled job: apply canary config to cluster/staging-usw2 at 2024-09-18T02:15:00Z (eta 5m).
